title: France's tax administration reports that its Foncier innovant tool found 140,000 taxable swimming pools in 2023, and another section of its report gives more than 120,000
summary: Foncier innovant, a tool of France's tax administration that detects pools in aerial photographs, found 140,000 taxable pools in 2023, which the administration values at €40 million in local tax.
account: In October 2021 the Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), France's tax administration, introduced Foncier innovant, an algorithmic tool. The tool detects pools and buildings on IGN aerial photographs and compares them with declarations. An agent then checks each detection. In 2022 an experiment in nine départements found 20,000 pools (20 Minutes, 12 June 2024). On 2 June 2023 the DGFiP announced that Foncier innovant would cover all of metropolitan France in 2023. On 20 March 2024 Thomas Cazenave, minister for public accounts, presented the first assessment of the government's anti-fraud plan at Bercy. He said that the tool had detected 140,000 undeclared swimming pools. He said that this would let local authorities collect about €40 million in property tax. Owners received DGFiP letters asking them to regularize their declarations (RMC, Ouest-France, L'Indépendant, 21 March 2024). In Ouest-France on 21 March 2024, Olivier Vilois of the CGT Finances publiques union said that, according to colleagues in the field, the algorithms' error rate stood at 55 to 60% at the time. L'Indépendant gave a figure of 120,000 for 2022, so the press accounts of the yearly split disagree. On 24 March 2024 ici (France Bleu) reported on the Dordogne public-finance office. It had found about 1,500 undeclared pools in 2023 among some 30,000 in the département. The office would send notices to catch up on property tax by the end of March. CNews (11 June 2024) cites the DGFiP annual activity report as reported by Ouest-France. It gives 140,000 pools identified in 2023 and €40 million that should have been paid in 2023. In its section on pool controls, the DGFiP's 2023 annual report gives 140,000 taxable pools in 2023, compared with 20,000 in 2022, and €40 million in additional local property-tax revenue. The report's separate cadastral overview gives more than 120,000 pools, and the report leaves the difference unresolved. The sources give no result for individual communes. In October 2024 the Cour des comptes reported that Foncier innovant raised the number of taxed pools in the nine pilot départements by 5.7%, or 20,356 pools. The Cour reported that the tool brought in €4.4 million in recurring revenue and €5.7 million in back-tax in 2022. The Cour added that the €40 million for 2023 is a DGFiP estimate, and it found that the tool produces many false positives that agents must clear. In April 2026 the DGFiP extended the campaign to verandas and garages with a €100 million goal (France 2).
purpose: Detect undeclared pools and buildings from aerial imagery so that they are added to the cadastral base and taxed. This was the tool's intended purpose.
system: Foncier innovant (DGFiP deep-learning detection of pools and buildings on IGN aerial photographs, built with Capgemini and Google)
developer: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) with Capgemini and Google
deployer: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), ministère de l'Économie et des Finances
domain: Public finance: property-tax base and anti-fraud
taxonomy_note: Tax yield is read as the authority's revenue; Trustible's description is written for product sales.

ratings.reason: Owners of detected pools bear a cost, and no individual beneficiary is documented.

The DGFiP estimates that the tool added about €40 million in local property tax for 2023. The Cour des comptes reports €4.4 million in recurring revenue and €5.7 million in back-tax from the 2022 pilot. In Dordogne alone the public-finance office is recovering tax on about 1,500 pools.
About €40 million nationally is small against total property-tax receipts. The DGFiP's own report gives 140,000 pools in one section and more than 120,000 in another.

ai_role.statement: Foncier innovant extracted pool outlines from IGN aerial images and compared them with tax declarations. Tax officers systematically verified anomalies before contacting owners. DGFiP’s 2023 annual report states that 140,000 taxable pools were detected in 2023, compared with 20,000 in 2022, representing€40 million in additional local property-tax revenue. A separate overview in the report says more than 120,000 pools. The figures are the deploying administration’s account, not an independent error-rate evaluation.

fields.account: In October 2021 the Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), France's tax administration, introduced Foncier innovant, an algorithmic tool. The tool detects pools and buildings on IGN aerial photographs and compares them with declarations. An agent then checks each detection. In 2022 an experiment in nine départements found 20,000 pools (20 Minutes, 12 June 2024). On 2 June 2023 the DGFiP announced that Foncier innovant would cover all of metropolitan France in 2023. On 20 March 2024 Thomas Cazenave, minister for public accounts, presented the first assessment of the government's anti-fraud plan at Bercy. He said that the tool had detected 140,000 undeclared swimming pools. He said that this would let local authorities collect about €40 million in property tax. Owners received DGFiP letters asking them to regularize their declarations (RMC, Ouest-France, L'Indépendant, 21 March 2024). In Ouest-France on 21 March 2024, Olivier Vilois of the CGT Finances publiques union said that, according to colleagues in the field, the algorithms' error rate stood at 55 to 60% at the time. L'Indépendant gave a figure of 120,000 for 2022, so the press accounts of the yearly split disagree. On 24 March 2024 ici (France Bleu) reported on the Dordogne public-finance office. It had found about 1,500 undeclared pools in 2023 among some 30,000 in the département. The office would send notices to catch up on property tax by the end of March. CNews (11 June 2024) cites the DGFiP annual activity report as reported by Ouest-France. It gives 140,000 pools identified in 2023 and €40 million that should have been paid in 2023. In its section on pool controls, the DGFiP's 2023 annual report gives 140,000 taxable pools in 2023, compared with 20,000 in 2022, and €40 million in additional local property-tax revenue. The report's separate cadastral overview gives more than 120,000 pools, and the report leaves the difference unresolved. The sources give no result for individual communes. In October 2024 the Cour des comptes reported that Foncier innovant raised the number of taxed pools in the nine pilot départements by 5.7%, or 20,356 pools. The Cour reported that the tool brought in €4.4 million in recurring revenue and €5.7 million in back-tax in 2022. The Cour added that the €40 million for 2023 is a DGFiP estimate, and it found that the tool produces many false positives that agents must clear. In April 2026 the DGFiP extended the campaign to verandas and garages with a €100 million goal (France 2).

value.text: The tool has run since October 2021, and the Cour des comptes reports €4.4 million in recurring revenue from the 2022 pilot. The DGFiP reports 140,000 taxable pools for 2023. In April 2026 the DGFiP extended the campaign to verandas and garages with a goal of €100 million, according to France 2.

The Cour added that the €40 million for 2023 is a DGFiP estimate, and it found that the tool produces many false positives that agents must clear. In April 2026 the DGFiP extended the campaign to verandas and garages with a €100 million goal (France 2).
